comment_grading:
Homework 10%(best 3 of 4) 
Group Project 15%

Final 45%  
As I mentioned in my title, this is a risky course with an unclear grading. Let’s break everything down and talk about the details. 
Homework: Homework is manageable if you refer to lecture notes and collaborate with classmates. They tend to use the same homework questions every semester so asking students who took this course previously is helpful. However, some homework questions are not clear enough for students to understand its meaning. The grading is weird, in a way that even if TAs pointed out your mistakes, deduction in marks may not be necessary. 
Group project: The group project is one of the drawbacks in this course as it brings about some uncertainties. In the group project, a group of 5 or 6 is required to solve a real-world problem with methods regarding IEDA (not necessary to be the materials provided in this semester). Normally, students have to start working on that 1 month before the presentation, which is on the last 2 lectures of this course. The first thing is the choice of the topic. More than half of the group chose issues related to UST. After that, survey is required for some group as data base for research. In our group, some data are made-up since it’s not reasonable compared to the fact. After calculation base on data, conclusion can be drawn. Then, the preparation of presentation is available. The grading is based on the presentation with some requirements. Some important requirements are that everyone in the group has to present and the time for the presentation should be less than12 minutes.  
Exams: Exam paper consists of 10 MCs and 4 or 5 LQs with midterm covering L1-L6 and final covering L5-L9. A page of double-sided A4 cheat sheet is allowed in the exams. A sample paper is provided before the exams. A try of sample paper is worthwhile since some of the MCs in the exams are the same as that in the sample paper. The midterm questions are a little weird compared to the exercise and homework but still manageable with a high mean. The final is more difficult than the midterm becuase the process of LQs are more complicated with abundant calculations. 
Remark: Same as previous semesters, grade of group project and final weren't released officially. In my opinion, this behaviour is irresponsible for students who have the right to get notified of their academic performance. What’s more, my friend and I both got a grade that is a subgrade lower than our anticipation and as you may notice from other reviews that the grading is harsh in recent 2 semesters. So, if you really mind your grade, don’t enrol in this course. Take it easy and accept your B/C range grade if you are confident enough to get an A/B range.
comment_workload: The workload before midterm is light with 3 assignments which can be finished within 2 hours. However, as much work is needed for the project, students need to spend 2-3 hours a week for it with the probability in occurrence of free rider.

Organizational structures that foster innovation, including the impact of firm size, formalization, centralization, and balancing creativity with efficiency (Part 6)
The shift from closed to open innovation paradigms, emphasizing external collaboration and crowdsourcing (Part 7).

comment_teaching:
1. The Life stories:
As others have mentioned, the professor sometimes will start talking about his personal life during the lectures. These stories may seem to be off topic. SOME do relate to the teaching material. For example: 
Teaching topic at the time:
Just-In-Time Inventory, where we should keep inventory as low as possible to reduce waste and force process improvement.
Life Stories: 
Many years ago, he gave his sons 1000 dollar allowance. Then he cut it by 10% each week. If his son can live without the 10% he continues, until his son starts complaining.
How they link:
When the son complains, the minimum allowance amount is found just like lowering inventory reveals hidden inefficiencies in operations.
There are some life stories that is not related at all like how he saw combs of bananas being on discount at 3 HKD in Fusion so he bought a lot and now eats 2 bananas a day. Did you know you can preserve bananas by covering them in plastic wrap?
Overall, the life stories and jokes, made the long lectures less boring and tiring. I personally prefer this type of teaching. Its way better than him just throwing knowledge at us without making it relatable.
2. Lecture Structure:
9:30 - 11:00 Talks about the main slides

As you can see, this 2-week course is divided into 2 parts, the first half about technology and the second half about policies. Whoever designed this course for some reason thought that cramming 18923791283 things into 2 weeks is a good idea, which leads to this super intense schedule.
The first half started off by briefly going through the whole ELEC1200 and DSE ICT networking unit (not joking) in the first 2 lectures, then moved onto introducing many, MANY new telecommunication technologies to you, talking about their working principles very briefly and mainly focusing on their societal and business impacts. This half is honestly pretty fun for technology enjoyers, and is really easy if you have studied related courses before.
I only went to like 2 lectures after the midterm due to being busy organizing Firebird CTF (please join COMP2633), so I could not really say much about the second half of the course. The second half is all about business theories, with a ton of easy concepts and terms that you can understand effortlessly but would take you a lot of time to remember that they exist. The economics theories are pretty tough for me to handle since I have never studied DSE economics back in secondary school, but there were not many of them and they did not appear in the final exam anyways. Overall speaking, the second half is really easy if you have studied some economics before, and the rest is basically just a bunch of terms and concepts added onto common sense. It is quite boring for me, but I think it would be more fun had I actually watched the lecture videos.

This looks like a fairly positive review so far, right? Well, I have to say, I ABSOLUTELY HATED THIS COURSE. I was NEVER a single day happy with this course, and only realized I fell into a REALLY DEEP rabbit hole when the midterm comes. This leads us to the worst part of this course: grading.

Fill-in-the-blanks questions sometimes went completely out of context to the point that you have to pray to God and ask for directions. The short question was literally disguised to be an essay, which at first gave you an impression that you could write whatever you want and you will get full mark as long as your points all make sense. However, the marking scheme said you only need to LIST OUT 2 exact points that the professor wanted and you get a HUGE mark deduction if you did not. Last time I saw such a similar exam was ~2 years ago when I was doing my DSE ICT paper 1, which shows how terrible the paper was. Half of the marks that I lost were from MCs, while the other half was from the short question. I know this is much of a skill issue, but it does little to affect my opinion on the paper.
The final exam is more business-oriented, so the portion of short questions become larger. The short questions are usually the part which lowers the mean by a lot, but this year they decided to put the EASIEST short questions that I have ever seen, which raised the bar a lot higher than previous years.
Statistics of final exam: (they decided to release it this year)
Mean: 84.29/100, SD: 7.16
My score: 91/100
Remember when 66.5 marks was the mean of the final exam? NOT ANYMORE! The paper was the same difficulty as the midterm assignment, and the only reason why the mean is slightly lower is that not all people could not put 500 slides of content onto a single A4 paper (most of the people managed to do this by setting the font size to like 0.0000000001, I have no idea how they could read that). The short questions were SO EASY to the point that you just have to copy points from the lecture notes and use a little bit of your common sense to score you high marks. The MC wordings are still vague and the fill-in-the-blanks are EVEN MORE GUESSY than the ones in midterm assignment, which really makes me question my life and regret not dropping the course 1238971239123 times during the 3 hours i was in front of the paper.
To illustrate how bad the exam format of this course actually is, I should probably talk about my personal experiences first. The night before the final exam, I was rushing my cheatsheet and did not sleep at all, so I was super tired and my brain completely turned off. The worst thing of all is I literally fell asleep while doing the paper. I had no idea how long I slept, but even with such a terrible body condition into the exam, I still managed to finish the exam with AROUND 1.5 HOURS TO SPARE. The majority of the students finished their paper in around an hour or so and decided to leave early, so the classroom went from fully seated at the start of the exam to more than half empty towards the end. I did not want to leave early, so I literally wrote explanations on the question paper next to every MC question. To lengthen my short questions to make myself look like I was thinking, I kept repeating my points and paraphrasing them until all the answers went out of the answer boxes. Even after all these meaningless actions, I still had enough time to thoroughly check my entire paper a few more times.
The exam format, as you can see, is extremely frustrating. The course gives you an 3-hour exam paper which you can finish in 1.5 hours to waste your precious time, and just completely destroys your confidence and hard work by grading the short questions according to a not-so-reasonable marking scheme. I guess this might be more of a personal issue and massive skill issue (again), but I really believe the assessment part is what singlehandedly pulls the quality of the course down.
The ideas of open Internet unlimited time midterm assignment and printed cheatsheet without regulation in the final exam are pretty bad for distinguishing the students as well. In the midterm assignment, all you need to do is to copy the question and paste it onto the browser, and you will get so many useful answers that you can immediately copy and paste into your assignment. You can even directly ask questions on Chegg and websites like that so you can get full mark as long as you pay for it! In the final exam, everyone just decided to copy every single slide onto 1 A4 paper so they can copy whatever and whenever they want! Does this really show that they have learnt stuff from the course? NO! These 2 things along with easy assessments are the main culprits as to why this course's mean is always so high. The exams are not about understanding, but are about copying and copying only. Whoever copies the fastest gets A+ despite not learning a single thing from this course! Meanwhile, the ones who worked hard and understands everything get C instead. Why not actually design fairly fun and challenging exam papers that requires thinking instead?
The only thing that keeps the rating from being a solid E is the fact that the final grade has not been assigned yet. There are reviews that say +1 SD is still B+, which means the grading is rather harsh; On the other hand, there are also reviews that say the professor gives maximum A range, which means the grading is fairly good. I know my score is completely out of A range already, which is something that I expected coming into this course, so it is really just a test of whether I will get B+, B or B-. Will come back to update this review after the letter grade is out.
Update: My final grade is A, which is extremely surprising as the grading is really lenient this year. However, please check the comments before thinking that this is a good grade course. This course's grading is VERY inconsistent and unpredictable, so please think twice before enrolling in this course.
In conclusion, I strongly DO NOT suggest anyone who cares about their CGA to study this course, as this course is straight up brutal in terms of competition, and A range will be difficult to get no matter how good you are. However, if you just want to take an SA common core out of your way without caring how bad your TGA in winter will be, this course is a very good choice. The shorter the pain, the better.

comment_workload:
Why are people saying the workload is light for this course, I'd say it's heavier than other CC's at least if you want to score higher/be on her good side.
Before every lecture you are "expected" to pre-read the lecture notes, watch the pre-lecture videos and read the pre-lecture articles. In class, as discussed in the teaching portion, students are expected to engage in discussion for participation marks by answering questions or showing their perspectives on an open-ended task. Attendance is not mandatory, but as usual they highly "recommend" people attend all lectures. 
The two essays are just 250 words each, and if you write any topic related to marketing or its effects you could probably get full marks for both essays.
In terms of the presentation, the workload really depends on your groupmates. Those who do not know any people in the class are assigned random teammates (otherwise you could work with your friends), so if there are any freeriders in your group your workload may be higher. Generally, my group was pretty good as two of my groupmates were Marketing students and were willing to contribute a lot, so my workload throughout the presentation and project was quite manageable.
The final quiz, held during the last teaching week of the semester, is comprised of 24 MCQ's and one open-ended question regarding the evaluation of an ad campaign. In my opinion, the quiz really only benefits those who attend the lecture and pays attention to the supporting material. The quiz included some very specific memorization-based questions (like how many SDG's are there or what is the triple bottom line in a social business), but also a lot of conceptual questions (like what is this ad trying to say about this concept), which has answers that could only be understood if you not only were in-class, but participating in-class. No matter how obscure some of the lecture information is, there is always a chance she WILL test that (like asking what marketing campaign did the Chinese history museum did to raise more funds, which I hardly remember if we ever went over in-class). NOTE: DO remember to watch the videos that were given as pre-reading or shown in-class! They accounted for around 60% of the MCQ's (they literally ask "In the TED Talk about this topic by this person" frequently). The open-ended question was a bit easier, as they'd show an ad related to a major topic of the course, and ask whether the ad could attract new customers/raise brand and market value/make a difference etc. You have 220 words to list your answer and give reasons supporting your answer and you are evaluated based on whether your ideas were logical and relavent (no right or wrong answer); it's like writing an English examination but with Marketing concepts. 
In general, if you want to score high on the quiz, the amount of active engagement you need to do in-class and studying out-of class is equally as high. So I would definitely NOT say this course has a "low" workload, especially towards the end.
